problem: Given that $P(A)=0.4,$ $P(B)=0.3,$ and $P(A\cap B)=0.1,$ find $P({A}^{′}\cup B).$

feedback.problem: Given that $P(A)=0.5,$ $P(B)=0.3,$ and $P(A\cup B)=0.7,$ find $P({A}^{′}\cup B).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $P(A\cap B)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ 0.7 & =0.5+0.3-P(A\cap B) \\ P(A\cap B) & =0.5+0.3-0.7 \\ P(A\cap B) & =0.1\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we construct the corresponding Venn diagram and shade the region ${A}^{′}\cup B.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14041480/assets/14e573701578699d9c0fa5c0aa8f97d2c20fc916e867d0c89d3fe1256feccf69.png)

Finally, we have

$$
P({A}^{′}\cup B)=0.1+0.2+0.3=0.6.
$$
